A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same framework, and their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. The supplied v1 ends after its references; v2 adds supplementary Sections 6–8. No material extraction gaps prevented comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original motion-generation experiments, including sparse control, goal-driven synthesis, implicit constraints, runtime and robustness evaluations in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds sampling results in Table 9 and generated-motion examples in Figures 6–7.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same two-stage diffusion framework, mask imputation, implicit noise optimization and time-agnostic alignment objective. The supplement documents architecture and body-shape conditioning already described in v1; it does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: HumanML3D and the reaching, climbing and sitting datasets remain unchanged. Section 8 adds qualitative scenarios involving manually specified challenging trajectories and more expressive prompts, including stair climbing and complex backward walking. The detailed goal-dataset descriptions do not establish new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain CondMDI, OmniControl, TLControl, MotionLCM, DNO and the existing ablated variants. Section 6.2 newly documents checkpoint use and CondMDI training, without establishing revised comparators. Table 9 expands sampling configurations of existing variants.

E3.justification: Table 9 extends the 10-step DDIM sparsity evaluation beyond v1's r = 30 setting to r = 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 and 60. The shared experiments retain their protocols. Newly supplied training, preprocessing and split details in Section 6 are disclosures rather than demonstrated setting changes.

E4.justification: Section 7 expands sampler sensitivity analysis with DDIM10 across sparsity levels and additional DDIM5 metrics. Section 8 adds challenging-trajectory robustness examples and expressive-prompt case studies. Table 9 also repeats existing DDPM results, and some DDIM5 findings were already plotted in v1's Figure 5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. The added results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 and Figure 5 retain their results. Table 9 adds results such as DDIM10 at r = 60: FID 0.297, control error 0.041 m and R-precision 0.661, plus previously unreported auxiliary metrics for DDIM5. Figures 6–7 add qualitative outcomes; these are additional results, not demonstrated improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, diffusion losses and arc-length alignment derivation remain unchanged. Figure 2 repeats existing dimensional definitions, while Table 8 documents a standard diffusion variance setting. No new theoretical assumptions, propositions or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: decomposed diffusion synthesis, precise sparse keyjoint control and flexible constraints including time-agnostic and goal-driven control.

C2.justification: Section 8 newly interprets the manual-trajectory examples as evidence of generalization to unseen, difficult constraints and the complex-prompt examples as evidence of expressive semantic control. Existing explanations of decomposition and the limitation that the method is not real-time remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Sections 6.1–6.3 and Table 8 supply substantial previously unavailable reproduction details: optimizer and hyperparameters, model widths, diffusion settings, baseline checkpoints and training, body-shape features, and goal-data extraction, augmentation, sample counts and normalization. v1 deferred these details to supplementary material absent from its supplied PDF. One ambiguity remains: Section 6.1 associates 128 channels with the full-body model, whereas Table 8 lists 512.

R1.justification: Seven references are added, covering Less Is More, SnapMoGen, Goal-driven Human Motion Synthesis in Diverse Task, SceneMI, DDPM, AdamW and improved DDPM. These extend citation coverage and support implementation details; the related-work organization and central novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 appends supplementary Sections 6–8 and acknowledgements, expands the affiliation and makes small wording corrections. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially unchanged, without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds the hyperparameter and sampling tables (Tables 8–9) and two qualitative figure panels (Figures 6–7). Figure 2's caption gains dimensional annotations, Figure 3 moves within page 6, and text reflows. Existing main figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies implementation and dataset details that v1 referenced but did not include, making the experiments easier to assess and reproduce. Expanded sampling results and qualitative tests provide useful supporting evidence while the principal findings remain unchanged. The benefit is tempered by the new channel-width inconsistency between Section 6.1 and Table 8.
